sources.role: official source archive; src/vm/mz2500, config.cpp, win32/winmain.cpp and win32/osd_input.cpp
official Windows x64 executable and distribution evidence
official EmuZ-2500 Win32 readme and ROM/key map

paths.naming: Win32 load_config/save_config call create_local_path("mz2500.ini"). [Control] persists BootMode, OptionSwitch, MonitorType, CorrectDiskTiming/IgnoreDiskCRC and tape settings; [RecentFiles] persists floppy, hard-disk and tape paths; [Input] persists JoyButtonsEx1_1..JoyButtonsEx8_16 and JoyToKey settings.

The WinMM backend enumerates joystick IDs 0..3 at runtime and uses JoyButtonsEx values encoded as (joystick_index << 5) | direction/button/axis/POV bit. JoyToKeyButtons negative values encode Windows virtual keys; UseJoyToKey, JoyToKeyType and JoyToKeyNumPad5 are persisted in [Input]. The MZ-2500 VM consumes joystick 0/1 for its two joystick ports and also has a serial mouse device. keycode.cfg is an optional 256-byte VK-to-DIK table, not a stable controller identity.

paths.path: <directory containing mz2500.exe>\MZ-1R12.BIN for the optional MZ-1R12 32 KiB SRAM; attached floppy/hard-disk/tape media remain at their user-selected paths. If no hard-disk path exists, the VM defaults to <directory containing mz2500.exe>\SASI0.DAT and SASI1.DAT.
paths.naming: MZ-1R12.BIN is read at startup and written on VM release only when SRAM changed. Floppy images and SASI hard-disk images are guest filesystems, not Lunchbox sidecars; [RecentFiles] stores the selected paths.

paths.naming: Ten Win32 menu slots call state_file_path(n), formatting <CONFIG_NAME>.sta<n>. The stream includes the common outer/config state and the complete MZ-2500 device graph; it is version/build-bound (outer state version 3, config-state version 8) rather than a portable interchange format.

paths.path: <directory containing mz2500.exe>\IPL.ROM and KANJI.ROM (required baseline); optional device ROMs include KANJI2.ROM, DICT.ROM, PHONE.ROM, MZ1E18.ROM/MZ-1E18.ROM, MZ1E30.ROM/MZ-1E30.ROM/SASI.ROM/FILE.ROM, MZ1E32.ROM/MZ-1E32.ROM and the MZ-1R13 dictionary variants.
paths.naming: The official EmuZ-2500 readme states IPL.ROM and KANJI.ROM are required. Source loads those plus optional device files from the executable directory; option switches select MZ-1E26, MZ-1E30, MZ-1E32, MZ-1R12, MZ-1R13, MZ-1R37 and W3100A emulation. No canonical checksums are published for the user-supplied ROMs.

paths.path: No cryptographic or firmware-key file is used by EmuZ-2500.
paths.naming: keycode.cfg is an input scan-code conversion table and belongs to the input disposition; ROMs are firmware assets, not decryption keys.
evidence: source:http://takeda-toshiya.my.coocan.jp/common/source.7z sha256=63d598a29cabf2d9212bd8a1699d8bcddf2416e711c20581a0d665c96f2399 (MZ-2500 target has no cryptographic key handling)

windows.notes: The official x64 artifact is a PE32+ Windows executable. Lunchbox has no verified native controller writer for this Windows-only target; it must not modify a user's mz2500.ini or keycode.cfg.

linux.reason: The official Common Source Code Project distribution provides Windows Win32/x64 artifacts and source with a Win32 frontend, but no verified native Linux EmuZ-2500 package.

linux-flatpak.reason: No official EmuZ-2500 Flatpak package or manifest is published by the Common Source Code Project.

macos.reason: The official Common Source Code Project distribution provides Windows Win32/x64 artifacts and no verified native macOS EmuZ-2500 package.
